doc.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Pianists students should listen to
summary: Hyman recommends Tatum, Oscar Peterson, Bill Evans, James P. Johnson and Teddy Wilson.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Suppose we had some budding college musicians watching you right now and instructors sometimes give them lists of people to listen to. If you had to pick two or three, and they are aspiring jazz musicians —
Well would you say they’re aspiring jazz pianists?

Okay. Well then they ought to hear the greatest jazz pianist, who is Art Tatum. I would say they have to hear Art Tatum, they have to hear Oscar Peterson of course, and they have to hear Bill Evans, and they have to hear older stuff too: James P. Johnson, Teddy Wilson, that would be enough to start with. And that’s of course in addition to what I imagine such people would already be interested in, I assume that they would know all about Chick Corea and Herbie Hancock and people more recent even than those two. But I’m saying of the music of the past, which I think is very important in order to play the present correctly.
